sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our twenties,
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《二十岁心理学》，这是一档探讨我们二十岁时的重大变化、时刻与转变，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些变化对我们心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our twenties.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们将继续剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: I have a very fun, or at least I think it's fun, very fascinating at least, in-depth science episode for you all today about the big hunk of flesh in your skull, your brain.
sentences.zh: 今天我要为大家带来一期非常有趣（至少我认为很有趣，而且至少非常迷人）、深入探讨科学的节目，主角就是你头骨里那个厚重的肉团——你的大脑。

sentences.en: I think most of us know a few interesting facts about the brain.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大多数人都对大脑有一些有趣的了解。

sentences.en: We know it's 75% water, that there are things called neurons and synapses.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它有 75% 的水分，知道有神经元和突触这东西。

sentences.en: Maybe you can even label the four major lobes if you paid close enough attention in year 10 biology.
sentences.zh: 如果你在十年级的生物课上足够认真，你甚至能说出大脑四个主要叶的名称。

sentences.en: But do you actually understand why your brain behaves the way it does?
sentences.zh: 但你真的理解为什么你的大脑会有这样的行为吗？

sentences.en: Why you can remember an embarrassing moment from 12 years ago, but forget what you had for breakfast yesterday?
sentences.zh: 为什么你能记住 12 年前一件尴尬的事情，却忘记了昨天早餐吃的是什么？

sentences.en: And certain habits seem impossible to break, whilst others you don't have to try very hard for.
sentences.zh: 某些习惯似乎根本无法改掉，而另一些习惯你却毫不费力。

sentences.en: These are all questions to do with your brain, and to do with how this thing in your head is structured and works.
sentences.zh: 这些都是关于你大脑的问题，也关于你脑海里这个东西是如何结构化和运作的。

sentences.en: The more neuroscience I read, the more humbled I become, because every thought you have, every memory you keep, every emotion you feel, even pain, every decision you make,
sentences.zh: 我阅读的神经科学越多，就越感到自身的渺小，因为你的每一个思想、你保留的每一段记忆、你感受到的每一种情绪（甚至疼痛）、你做出的每一个决定，

sentences.en: is the product of an organ weighing just over a kilo that somehow manages to build your entire experience of reality.
sentences.zh: 都是一个仅重一公斤多一点的器官的产物，而它却不知何故设法构建了你对现实的整个体验。

sentences.en: And yet most of us go through life knowing surprisingly very little.
sentences.zh: 然而我们大多数人对它的了解少得惊人，就这样度过了一生。

sentences.en: So today I wanted to do something a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想做点不一样的。

sentences.en: Rather than just focusing on one psychological concept, we are going to explore seven of the most surprising and genuinely useful facts about your brain that you may not know.
sentences.zh: 与其只关注单一的心理学概念，不如让我们来探索关于大脑的七个最令人惊讶且真正有用的事实，这些可能是你不知道的。

sentences.en: And even if you do, provide a little bit more of the little known research behind those facts, just to give you something interesting to talk about at dinner parties,
sentences.zh: 即使你知道，我也要提供这些事实背后的、鲜为人知的一点研究，不仅能为你的晚宴派对提供一些有趣的话题，

sentences.en: but also so that you understand yourself better.
sentences.zh: 还能让你更好地了解自己。

sentences.en: More than that, I really do hope that you'll just leave with a greater appreciation for the genuine miracle that is your brain and how to take its quirks
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，我真的希望大家在听完后，能对大脑这个真正的奇迹有更多的赞赏，学会利用它的怪癖

sentences.en: and its strange idiosyncrasies and use them to your advantage.
sentences.zh: 和奇特特性来为自己谋取优势。

sentences.en: Without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，我们直接切入正题。

sentences.en: Let's come out of the gate strong.
sentences.zh: 让我们开局就放大招。

sentences.en: Number one, your brain can physically rewire itself.
sentences.zh: 第一点，你的大脑可以进行物理重塑。

sentences.en: Even if it's injured, even if entire parts of your brain are removed, you might have heard of the term neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 即使它受伤了，即使大脑的整个部分被切除，你可能也听说过“神经可塑性”这个词。

sentences.en: And this is exactly what we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们今天要讨论的。

sentences.en: A very good definition, probably the best definition of neuroplasticity I've come across is basically, it is the ability for your nervous system, including your brain,
sentences.zh: 一个非常好的定义，可能是我遇到过的关于神经可塑性的最佳定义，基本上就是：神经系统（包括大脑）

sentences.en: to change its activity in response to intrinsic and extrinsic stimuli by reorganizing its structures, its functions, its connections.
sentences.zh: 通过重组其结构、功能和连接，来响应内在和外在刺激并改变其活动的能力。

sentences.en: In other words, our brain can adapt due to experience.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们的大脑能够根据经验进行适应。

sentences.en: This is what allows us to learn new skills, to recover after strokes or traumatic brain injuries, and also to change our deep ways of being and our thought patterns and our habits.
sentences.zh: 这正是让我们能够学习新技能、在中风或创伤性脑损伤后恢复、以及改变我们深层的生存方式、思维模式和习惯的原因。

sentences.en: If we didn't have neuroplasticity, we wouldn't be capable of any kind of personal evolution.
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有神经可塑性，我们就无法进行任何形式的个人进化。

sentences.en: We wouldn't be capable of any kind of adaptation.
sentences.zh: 我们将无法进行任何形式的适应。

sentences.en: This is our brain's first superpower.
sentences.zh: 这是我们大脑的第一大超能力。

sentences.en: Our brain is very good at working out what we need and what we don't need.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑非常善于弄清楚我们需要什么和不需要什么。

sentences.en: It's a bit of an efficiency machine at its core.
sentences.zh: 它的核心本质上是一台效率机器。

sentences.en: And this is how it carries out that efficiency plan through neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 这就是它通过神经可塑性执行效率计划的方式。

sentences.en: The thing is, we didn't really know the neural basis of this until probably 60 years ago or so.
sentences.zh: 问题是，直到大约 60 年前左右，我们才真正了解这一现象的神经基础。

sentences.en: Our brains are composed of around 100 billion, billion with a B, neurons.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑由大约 1000 亿个（“亿”字用 B 开头）神经元组成。

sentences.en: And early researchers really thought that, you know, that kind of creation of new neurons stopped shortly after birth.
sentences.zh: 早期的研究人员真的认为，这种新神经元的产生在出生后不久就停止了。

sentences.en: And we now know that is not true.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在知道事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And that throughout our lives, we can reorganize pathways, we can create new connections.
sentences.zh: 在我们的一生中，我们可以重组通路，可以建立新的连接。

sentences.en: And in some cases, we can even create new neurons, especially in our late teens and in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，我们甚至可以产生新的神经元，尤其是在我们十多岁快结束和二十多岁的时候。

sentences.en: Now, there are two main types of neuroplasticity that are very important for you to know if you want to change anything about who you are as a person.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你想改变作为人的任何特质，有两主要类型的神经可塑性是你必须了解的。

sentences.en: Firstly is functional plasticity.
sentences.zh: 首先是功能性可塑性。

sentences.en: This is the brain's ability to move functions from a damaged area of the brain to another undamaged area.
sentences.zh: 这是大脑将功能从受损区域转移到另一个未受损区域的能力。

sentences.en: This is mainly in response to things like trauma, but I mean physical trauma.
sentences.zh: 这主要是为了应对创伤之类的情况，我指的是身体创伤。

sentences.en: It is the equivalent of riding your bike around a pothole to avoid falling in.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于骑自行车时为了避免掉进坑洼而绕着它骑。

sentences.en: And this happens in three ways.
sentences.zh: 这种情况可以通过三种方式发生。

sentences.en: So functional neuroplasticity has three ways of operating.
sentences.zh: 所以功能性神经可塑性有三种运作方式。

sentences.en: Neuronal unmasking.
sentences.zh: 神经元去掩蔽。

sentences.en: So basically the brain opens up dormant or backup synapses that were previously inactive to take over damaged tissue nearby.
sentences.zh: 基本上，大脑会开启休眠或备用的、先前处于非活动状态的突触，以接管附近受损的组织。

sentences.en: Axonal sprouting.
sentences.zh: 轴突发芽。

sentences.en: Undamaged neurons grow new nerve endings, known as axons, to reconnect with other pathways and to build kind of lost networks.
sentences.zh: 未受损的神经元会生长出称为轴突的新神经末梢，以便与其他通路重新连接，并重建某种程度上丢失的网络。

sentences.en: This is like the part of you that comes in and builds bridges that were, I guess, bombed.
sentences.zh: 这就像是你体内跑出来重建那些被轰炸过的桥梁的部分。

sentences.en: And then there's neural network adaptation.
sentences.zh: 然后是神经网络适应。

sentences.en: Neighboring healthy regions become more engaged and take on new roles.
sentences.zh: 邻近的健康区域变得更加活跃并承担新的角色。

sentences.en: So we have reinforcements, bridge building, and then regional relocating.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有增援、建桥，还有区域搬迁。

sentences.en: I genuinely cannot explain how amazing it is that your brain can do that.
sentences.zh: 我真的无法形容你的大脑能做到这一点是多么令人惊叹。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm going to use the word miracle so many times, but it is almost miraculous that we have this entire task force of neurons dedicated to helping us survive
sentences.zh: 我觉得我会用无数次“奇迹”这个词，但我们拥有一支由神经元组成、专门帮助我们在经历可怕的事情、破坏性的事情时活下来

sentences.en: really awful things, damaging things, and to still function.
sentences.zh: 并继续运作的任务部队，这几乎是个奇迹。

sentences.en: Now the second way neuroplasticity takes place is through something called structural plasticity.
sentences.zh: 现在，神经可塑性发生的第二种方式是通过一种叫做结构性可塑性的东西。

sentences.en: Structural plasticity is the brain's ability to actually change its physical structure as a result of learning.
sentences.zh: 结构性可塑性是大脑因学习而实际改变其物理结构的能力。

sentences.en: And I don't just mean sitting down with a textbook learning, but learning through everyday life.
sentences.zh: 我指的不仅仅是坐在那里看教科书学习，而是通过日常生活进行学习。

sentences.en: Instead of just kind of changing the strength of existing signals or, you know, moving things around, it can physically alter its chemical and cellular makeup so that it looks
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是改变现有信号的强度或四处移动东西，它还能在物理上改变其化学和细胞构成，使其看起来

sentences.en: physically different.
sentences.zh: 在物理上有，所不同。

sentences.en: Certain areas of our brain can gain more volume and become more dense.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑的某些区域可以增加体积并变得更加密集。

sentences.en: And you can see this on brain imaging scans.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脑部成像扫描中看到这一点。

sentences.en: The more you learn or train or mentally challenge yourself, the more gray matter you may get.
sentences.zh: 你学习、训练或挑战自己的精神越多，你可能获得的灰质就越多。

sentences.en: And this is something that you can really do for most of your life.
sentences.zh: 这是你几乎可以在一生中持续做的事情。

sentences.en: That does kind of become a tipping point, but most of your life you get the density of your brain.
sentences.zh: 这确实会迎来一个拐点，但在你生命中的大部分时间里，你都在增加大脑的密度。

sentences.en: There are some limits to neuroplasticity, you know, for example, certain areas of your brain that are responsible for very specific actions can't be moved.
sentences.zh: 神经可塑性也是有一定局限性的，例如，你大脑中负责非常特定动作的某些区域是无法移动的。

sentences.en: So if the part of your brain that is responsible for language is severely damaged, this can't always be converted or part of your brain that's responsible for converting short-term
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你大脑中负责语言的部分严重受损，这并不总是能够转化；或者你大脑中负责将短期

sentences.en: to long-term memory is damaged.
sentences.zh: 记忆转化为长期记忆的部分受损了。

sentences.en: Again, it's not like we can rewire that completely.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们无法完全对其进行重新布线。

sentences.en: But in general, at nearly any stage of your life you can influence the flexibility of your brain, your neural networks, perhaps even the very structure of your brain
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，在你生命的几乎任何阶段，你都可以通过学习、通过行动、通过思想、通过练习对自己说的话或练习你所追求的目标、或者仅仅通过实践，

sentences.en: through learning and through your actions and also through your thoughts and what you practice telling yourself or what you practice striving for or just doing.
sentences.zh: 来影响大脑的灵活性、神经网络，甚至可能影响大脑的结构。

sentences.en: I think we believe that at some stage we just are the person we are and nothing's going to change about that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都曾认为，在某个阶段，我们就是现在的自己，对此没有任何东西会改变。

sentences.en: This is just who I always am going to be and neuroplasticity disproves this entirely.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子注定就是这样了，而神经可塑性彻底驳斥了这一点。

sentences.en: Your brain remains plastic for your entire life pretty much, especially if you give it the certain conditions under which to do so.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑几乎在你的一生中都保持着可塑性，特别是如果你为它提供这样做的特定条件的话。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about some very simple science-backed ways to actually promote neuroplasticity if you want to keep your brain in this malleable state.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谈谈一些非常简单、有科学依据的方法，如果你想让大脑保持这种可塑状态，可以借此来促进神经可塑性。
